name: qdoc preparation — option 2: one QDoc aggregate with invitations, approval in its own module
description: Direction of this option: one consolidated QDoc aggregate root that owns its versions and each version's invitations and assignments of authors, reviewers and approvers, with two separate lists of references per version: to its content files and to its attachments. There is no common file abstraction: content files and attachments differ in almost everything and live in modules of their own. Content management holds one ContentFile aggregate per content file with its body, revision, change history, comments and approval lock; its use cases ask drafting who may see, edit, comment or close comments through a VersionAccess port that drafting implements, so content management does not depend on drafting. The file store holds the attachments, immutable once stored and shared by the versions that reference them, with their quarantine and the scanning that activates or rejects them. The approval module holds one VersionReview aggregate per version with the reviewed marks and the per-approver approvals of content files and of attachments. The QDoc root checks every drafting invariant synchronously in one transaction: one version in preparation and one published at a time, at least one content file per version, at least one approver before sharing, an approved attachment stays in its version, archiving only with no version in force or in preparation, and no assignments or versions once archived. Approval checks only assigned approvers, no open comments, an active attachment and approval of exactly the revision seen, locks the approved content file or attachment and, at the last approval, marks the version approved, all in one transaction, so these rules stay strongly consistent. Each aggregate is saved under its own optimistic concurrency: authors editing one content file contend only with each other. People are assigned through invitations as on GitHub: the quality manager (or the auditor on own document) invites a person to a role on a version, the invitee accepts, and all assignment checks run at acceptance; a failed check refuses the assignment. The module tree is shallow under the root qdocmanagement, which also holds the shared QDocId, users, roles and PerformedBy: drafting holds the QDoc aggregate and its use cases, with the events it raises in its messages submodule; approval the review and approval of a version; numbering the <sequence>/<month>/<year> numbers with organisation prefix and suffix, demo prefix and auditor suffix; platform the supporting capabilities in four submodules: contentmanagement the content files and their comments, filestore the attachments and their scanning, activity the audit trail, written in the same transaction as the change, and notifications the e-mails. A failed attachment scan rejects the file in the file store, drafting removes it from the version as a system action, and the author is e-mailed. It gains strongly consistent invariants, a small QDoc, contention limited to one content file, and attachments stored once; it costs several aggregates changed together by the approval and file use cases, a port between content management and drafting, and an extra invitation step. Out of scope: late correction between approval and publication (the approval lock is absolute here; deferred to a later change), publication itself (it reaches drafting only as recordPublication and recordWithdrawal), attachment size limits (undecided pending research), tracking attachment downloads, and everything section 10 of the requirements lists: employee sign-off, templates, AI reviewers, other approval strategies, per-section approval and deletion.

description.value: QDoc management: the bounded context for quality documents (procedures, guidelines, instructions, policies) that organisations holding a quality certificate must maintain. description.value: Drafting of a QDoc: the QDoc aggregate that owns its versions, the invitations and assignments of each version, and for each version two lists of references: to its content files, stored in content management, and to its attachments, stored in the file store. The QDoc root checks every drafting invariant in one transaction, under optimistic concurrency on the whole aggregate. Its use cases create a QDoc and its versions, invite people, add and remove files, share and archive; adding a file creates it in its module and references it from the version in the same transaction. Drafting answers content management's question of who may do what with a version's content through QDocVersionAccess. Its events live in the messages submodule.

description.value: Review and approval of a version in preparation: the reviewers' "reviewed" marks and the per-approver approval of every content file and every attachment, up to the moment the version becomes approved. Approving a content file locks it in content management, approving an attachment locks it on the version in drafting, and the last approval marks the version approved, all in the same transaction, so every approval rule stays strongly consistent. Comments are not here: they live with the content file they are on.

description.value: The quality document as one aggregate: its versions (entities), each version's invitations and assignments, and each version's references to its content files and to its attachments. The files themselves are not part of it: content files, with their history, comments and lock, are ContentFile aggregates in content management; attachments, with their quarantine and scan, are Attachment aggregates in the file store. The root checks every drafting invariant synchronously in one transaction. The whole aggregate is saved under optimistic concurrency (concurrencyVersion): two commands that changed the same QDoc from the same starting point cannot both commit; the loser is rejected and retried on fresh state. Editing and commenting do not touch it, so they never contend with invitations or with each other across files. QDoc owns the consequences of approval that concern the version: the lock that keeps an approved attachment in it and the APPROVED status, both set by the approval module in the same transaction. Every change raises a QDoc event the activity list records.

description.value:
Issues the next sequence number of the organisation for the month of the creation date, reads the organisation's template, and assembles the document number: demo prefix, organisation prefix, core, organisation suffix, auditor suffix when the creator holds the auditor role and acts as such. Called by drafting when a QDoc is created, in the same transaction.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  QDocDraftingService->>DocumentNumberGenerator: generate(organisationId, creatorRoles, date)
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>MonthlySequenceRepository: findOrStart(organisationId, year, month)
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>MonthlySequence: issueNext()
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>MonthlySequenceRepository: save(sequence)
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>NumberTemplateRepository: findFor(organisationId)
```
